- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts — increase forecast by 3–5% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops in the first 5–7 days after a negative sentiment shift — apply a 2–3% upward bias to early forecast days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits mean reversion bias — adjust forecast to align with 30-day rolling mean of past 10–15 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates short-term volatility — reduce forecast by 1–2% for days 1–10 if sentiment is volatile or negative.
